reason: FAQ answer under 'Can I get a Windows or macOS-backed CloudShell?' states both parts verbatim: no Windows or macOS instances currently, PowerShell pre-installed and usable on Linux.
Quote states one virtual machine per Region per user, up to 10 sessions per virtual machine concurrently, and shells from multiple Regions open simultaneously; same scope and units as the claim.
First quote states the IAM-policy restriction and the Administrator/PowerUser default; second quote states that all other users must be granted permission by an administrator.

Quote 'same privileges as ... the AWS CLI on your local machine with the same credentials, no more, no less' entails the 'only' scope (the preceding context sentence says it verbatim); second quote states the CloudTrail logging and annotation.
Two quotes under Customization state both halves: inside the home directory persists, outside does not.
Quote states all three parts: stop after keyboard input inactivity, background processes are not activity and may be terminated without notice, all sessions disconnect when the console session ends.
First quote: common development and operations tools pre-installed, no need to install or configure software locally; second quote lists AWS CLI among the pre-installed CLIs.
Quote under 'Can I access resources in a VPC with CloudShell?' answers yes for resources in your private VPC.

Quote states Instance Connect connects to existing EC2 instances via a browser terminal, CloudShell needs no resources in the account, and CloudShell is most useful for AWS CLI commands and general purpose scripting.

The quote supports 'no additional charge' and 'you pay for other AWS resources', but the claim's third part, 'standard data transfer rates apply', is only in the context sentence that follows ('Moreover, standard data transfer rates also apply') and is not quoted as evidence.
Two quotes from the network restrictions list: outbound public internet access, no inbound ports, no public IP address.

Quote states home directory, private to you, persists between sessions unlike ephemeral resources recycled after each session; the per-Region scope is the preceding sentence of the same paragraph ('in each AWS Region').
Both quotes state 1 GB per Region at no cost in the home directory; the same paragraph states data in the home directory persists between sessions. 'max' matches 'up to 1 GB'.
Quote states the console Region is in sync with the CloudShell Region and that CloudShell operates in the nearest Region when unavailable in the selected one.
Quote under Security states Safe Paste is enabled by default and requires verifying that pasted multiline text has no malicious scripts.
Quote: a session running continuously for approximately 12 hours ends automatically even if the user is regularly interacting with it.
Quote states 20-30 minutes without keyboard or pointer interaction, 10 minutes in GovCloud (US), and that running processes do not count.

Quote states automatic deletion after 120 days unless you take action and that launching CloudShell again in that Region prevents removal; the context sentence sets the 'stop using in a Region' condition.
Quote states VPC environments have no persistent storage and $HOME is deleted on timeout, delete or restart; claim matches exactly.
Quote: only up to two VPC environments per IAM principal; same scope and maximum.

The claim and the display values are stated verbatim by the quote, but the spoken form of v1 ('the CLI is the same power from a terminal') makes a claim about the AWS CLI that the quote does not make; the page says nothing about the CLI.

Quote (Note in the Unified Settings procedure) states last-visited Region when no default is set, the IAM Identity Center advice, and that the last-visited Region does not persist across Identity Center sessions.

Quotes carry both values (Unified Settings page; Edit next to Localization and default Region); the remaining steps (gear icon, See all user settings, choose a Region, Save settings) are the numbered steps verbatim in the context.
Two quotes state the Services menu grouped by category, Unified Search, and the Favorites and Recently visited widgets on Console Home.
The quote conditions biometric sign-in on devices running Console Mobile Application v2.0+; the claim and the value drop that version condition.
Quote under 'Can I assume IAM roles?' answers 'Yes, on iOS and Android V2.0+'; the value display keeps that condition verbatim.
Quote states custom dashboards your identity may access are viewable and automatic dashboards are not yet supported; claim matches.
Quote states the only way to create resources is CloudShell with the AWS CLI, and the GUI allows view and sometimes modify but not create.
Two quotes: all FIDO certified hardware authenticators (e.g. YubiKey) for MFA, and the three named software authenticators.
Quote under 'Is MFA supported?' answers yes and recommends a hardware MFA device or a virtual MFA on a separate mobile device.
Quote states an IAM user can be deactivated after device loss and root accounts cannot be deactivated.
Quote states the app generates a pre-signed URL for an S3 object and that it grants time-limited permission to download the object.

Quotes state root, IAM user and federated login via AWS Single Sign-On, Microsoft Active Directory and third-party IdPs, and the recommendation of IAM user credentials or a federated role; the claim's 'IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS Single Sign-On)' is the RULINGS rule 6 current-name form of the quoted name.
Quote states usage charges are viewable, the Billing Preferences Receive Billing Alerts checkbox step, and the CloudWatch permission requirement.
Quote states the Solutions section features simplified and automated workflows and wizards that use and introduce services, and that they create the resources for the intended solution.

The quotes support the map view addition and the previous list-only state, but the date 2026-08-12 and 'all AWS Regions and Local Zones' appear only in the context ('Posted on: Aug 12, 2026'; 'all AWS Regions and AWS Local Zones plotted') and are not quoted as evidence.
Two quotes: the Local Zones tab in the Region selector shows all opted-in Local Zones, and clicking one opens its parent Region's console page.
Quote (Note on Choosing your Region) states both parts: the console may show a different Region, and some resources such as EC2 instances are Region specific.
Quote from the What's New post states up to 5 sessions in a single browser in any combination of root, IAM or federated roles in different or the same account.
Quote 'Opt-in is browser specific' sits in the Note that says you must opt in to multi-session support; both parts of the claim are stated.
